title: What to Expect at Black Hat USA 2026

segments.text: Hi everyone. I'm Susie Pallet, president
of Black Hat, and I'm really excited to
talk with you today about Black Hat USA
2026. We're less than 2 months out now.
The event runs August 1st through 6th at
Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, and honestly,
this is shaping up to be our most
dynamic year yet. I'm joined by two
people who've been instrumental in
building this year's experience. Steve
Oldenburg, our vice president of events,
and Laura Stebbing, our vice president
of content. We wanted to have a real
conversation with you about what makes
this year special, because when you're
choosing where to invest your time and
resources, you deserve to know exactly
what you're walking into. For 29 years,
Black Hat has been the place where the
cybersecurity community does its most
consequential work. And this year, we're
continuing to bring you brand new
research, cutting-edge training, and
some really innovative programming
reflects where the industry is right
now, not where it was last year or the
year before. Steve, when someone
registers for Black Hat, what's that
experience actually like from the moment
they commit to joining us?
>> You know, Susie, I think what people
don't always realize is that your Black
Hat experience really starts the moment
you register. You're not just buying a
pass, you're becoming part of a
community of over 20,000 practitioners,
researchers, and decision-makers who are
all coming together with the same goal.
And that's to stay one step ahead.
When you arrive in Las Vegas, you're
walking into the most technically
rigorous event in cybersecurity. There's
an energy to it, and that's hard to
describe until you've experienced it.
People come ready to learn, ready to
challenge assumptions, and ready to
connect with peers who understand the
work they're doing. Our trainings is
where so many so many people start their
Black Hat week. They run for four full
days, and we have over 100 expert-led
courses this year. But here's what makes
them different. These aren't lectures.
They're hyper-relevant, hands-on
experiences where you're actually
practicing practicing techniques you can
deploy when you get back to your desk.
Every instructor we bring in has used
these techniques in the in live
environments. They've been in the
trenches. So, you're not just learning
theory, you're building real deployable
skills under the guidance of people
who've actually done the work. And this
year we've significantly expanded our AI
security training track. The threat
landscape is shifting fast and your
capabilities need to shift with it.
We're focusing courses on securing LLMs,
defending against autonomous agents,
building detection pipelines that work
at machine speed. All the things that
are keeping practitioners up at night
right now.
>> It's such an important point, Steve. And
really segues, I suppose, neatly to the
research we're featuring this year. It's
not just recycled content or vendor
pitches, it's what's happening right now
in the field.
>> Exactly. And that brings us to
briefings, which really are at the heart
of the Black Hat Black Hat experience.
Briefings run August 5th and 6th, and
we're featuring over 100 peer-reviewed
research presentations.
This is where the community discovers
emerging threats before they hit vendor
white papers or mainstream press. And
what I really love about our process is
that every single briefing is selected
by an independent review board. So, not
sponsors, not by us. That rigor is why
practitioners keep coming back year
after year. They trust what they're
hearing on a Black Hat stage has been
vetted and it's worth their time.
This year's agenda, I have to say, is
incredible. We're covering everything
from AI agentic exploitation to
post-quantum cryptography, supply chain
attacks, next-gen detection engineering,
and the research you'll hear doesn't
exist in published form yet. You're
getting it first.
>> And the questions I love in these
environments are from the audience as
well, which are just as sharp as the
research itself, right?
>> Oh, yeah, absolutely. I mean, some of
the best learning happens in a Q&A. I'm
really excited about a few Q&As
this year. There's one that's the AI and
future of cyber defense, a panel hosted
by Michael Sulmeyer from Georgetown and
Katie Moussouris, CEO of Luta Security.
There's also the good, the bad, and the
ugly of AI security with Fred Hiding
from Harvard Kennedy School and Chris
Inglis, of course, the former US
National Security National Cyber
Director.
And Yuta Maeta from Wiz is presenting
the Crypto Cape exposing a sophisticated
multi-cloud bandit. These really are the
conversations that matter right now.
>> And if And if you have a Briefings Pass,
you also get access to something brand
new this year, which we're really
excited. It's a feature on our Business
Hall floor called the Interface. And
this is an immersive space designed to
turn passive observation into active
learning. We're talking hands-on demos,
scenario-based learning, live
challenges, expert-led sessions. It's
about getting your hands dirty and
really engaging with the material.
>> I love that we're creating more of those
opportunities for people to actually do
the work. So, not just watch the
presentations, but just do the work as
well.
>> Exactly. And speaking of hands-on, let's
talk about the Business Hall because
this year we've extended the hours and
added some exciting features. So, this
year the Business Hall opens Tuesday,
August 4th at 4:00 p.m. and will run
through Thursday, August 6th at 4:00
p.m. What makes it special is the
practitioners that walking around the
floor are coming straight out of our
Briefings and Trainings. They know what
questions to ask. They know what works
and what doesn't. Our 400-plus sponsors
and exhibitors we have this year
represent the top-tier tools and
solutions that actually hold up against
the practitioner scrutiny.
>> That is such a good point, Steve. It's
really not just vendor exposure, it's
evaluation as you go through it.
>> Absolutely correct. And we've added some
new spaces this year and new features
that I'm thrilled to share with you
today. The Convergence is a workspace
and networking area right in the middle
of the business hall where practitioners
can
come and compare notes between sessions,
connect with peers on similar problems,
and access career support from industry
leaders. We've also expanded our AI zone
which features early-stage companies
building the next generation of AI
security tools and Startup City. That's
where you'll see the companies that are
about to change the market. So, if you
want hands-on proof of concept, Arsenal
is where our researchers demonstrate
open-source tools live in real time
without any vendor polish. We have 89
in-person tool demonstrations in
addition to 20 dedicated Arsenal lab
sessions. Arsenal is where the community
comes together to demonstrate
capability, not just vendors
demonstrating product.
>> And rumor has it that our knock will
have a sibling this year?
>> Yes, so you're letting the cat out of
the bag and that is true. Our Black Hat
NOC, our network operations center,
we're adding a new feature to our floor
called the NOC Outpost. So, this will
give our attendees
additional time to come and connect with
our fantastic folks who help run our
secure and reliable network. So, as
we're going through and you're walking
the floor, make sure you go to the NOC
Outpost. There's going to be an
interesting feature there where you can
really learn about how to keep yourself
safe and protected on our black network.
>> I love that.
>> So, so much going on. Laura, we also
have summits
>> [laughter]
>> this year. I got excited about our
knockout post, which I know you and your
team have been working on. Tell us more
about those.
>> Yes, they are really exciting, too. So,
summits are running all day Tuesday,
August 4th, and we have six confirmed
programs. The CISO Summit, obviously
long-standing, the AI Summit, Innovators
and Investors Summit, the Financial
Threat Summit, our Healthcare Summit,
and the Omdia Analyst Summit. So, we've
got a lot going on.
And the thing about these is that
they're they're not just general
breakout sessions, they're full-day
domain-specific programs designed for
practitioners and executives with that
real deep focus in particular areas. So,
if you're a CISO, the CISO Summit is
where you really go to benchmark your
security posture against the best in the
field. Or if you're in building an AI
security strategy, the AI Summit is
where you pressure test your assumptions
with people that are doing that very
same work with you. So, the summits are
are really valuable because of who's in
the room and the room itself. You're not
in a general conference audience at all.
You're with peers who understand the
specific challenges you're facing.
>> And I believe we're bringing the Cyber
Warfare to Las Vegas, as well.
>> We are. So, after a really successful
launch at the Cyber Warfare Europe in
June, we're bringing Black Hat's Cyber
Warfare Forum series to Las Vegas.
And this is really an exclusive space
for senior cybersecurity leaders to
address nation-state campaigns,
AI-enabled operations, critical
infrastructure resilience, information
operations, and the legal and policy
frameworks that are shaping modern
conflict. And of course, it's all under
Chatham House Rules.
>> You know, I think beyond all the
technical programming, which we're known
for, Black Hat really though is about
the community. And this year we've built
in some moments that I think our our
attendees and people who are from the
community are going to love. We already
mentioned Arsenal Labs, 20 dedicated
sessions where you can
go hands-on with tools demonstrated in
Arsenal. But, we also have the drone
zone, which is where hacking literally
takes flight. It's a hands-on
cyber-physical security environment
focused on autonomous systems, drones,
robotics sensors machine-driven
decision-making.
You can observe, experiment, and
participate in real-world scenarios in a
controlled environment. Also, new is our
Cyber District, a dedicated space for
networking collaboration
and those conversations that happen when
you step away from the main stage.
>> And linked to that, we also have the
Black Hat Bar. Why don't you tell them
about
>> Yes.
>> Super excited to to let people know
about our Black Hat Bar and cafes
throughout the venue because, honestly,
some of the best conversations happen
over coffee, sometimes drinks, and not
just in a session room, right? There's
something really special. On Wednesday
night, we're also premiering Midnight in
the War Room, a documentary that takes
you inside real-world response to a
major cyber incident. It's powerful
storytelling that I think will resonate
with everyone.
>> 100%. It's going to be amazing. And, of
course, we can't forget our keynotes and
love notes.
>> So, keynotes is where we set the tone.
We introduce the big ideas,
the emerging threats, and really those
questions that the industry needs to be
asking. Love notes close the show on
Thursday afternoon. It's where we
reflect on what we've learned, what
surprised us, and what the community
really needs to take forward when they
leave Black Hat.
>> I want to build a little bit on what
Steve was saying about in terms of the
community. So, we're really highlighting
the community building moments we've
intensely designed this year, as well.
If this is your first Black Hat, we have
a first-timers welcome reception just
for you. This way you'll meet people
who've been coming for years and I think
Steve will tell you what to prioritize,
what not to miss, how to make the most
of your week. We're also really proud to
launch Black Hat Her this year and
networking initiative to give voice and
create space for women in cybersecurity.
And this is where we will celebrate the
women lead in the field and having the
conversations that really do need to
happen.
>> Yeah, and those conversations
community conversations are happening at
the convergence. As we mentioned, it's a
new on the floor
and those conversations are going to be
open forums where the community debates
the issues that matter. No panels, no
presentations, just practitioners
talking to practitioners.
>> Then throughout the week there are ask
me any things, networking receptions,
and those spontaneous conversations that
happen. With more than 20,000 people who
care deeply about the same things are
all in the same place. We're lucky we
know the magic of Black Hat, but here's
the thing for you, Black Hat USA 2026 is
the event that matters. When you're
making decisions about where to invest
your time, your energy, your
professional development, this is it.
And we're just weeks away. So, regular
registration pricing is active through
July 17th and then the prices do go up.
If you're serious about staying ahead,
which we know you all are, this is where
you need to be. You can register at
blackhat.com. We definitely can't wait
to see you in Las Vegas.
>> I'll see you there everyone.
>> Looking forward to it.
